text_html: A 38-year-old man comes to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of severe left lower abdominal pain. He has a history of pyelonephritis. His temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F). Abdominal examination shows tenderness to palpation over the left lower quadrant but no rebound tenderness or guarding. Leukocyte count is 12,000/mm3. An axial CT scan of the abdomen is shown. The most likely cause of the findings in this patient is abnormal migration and fusion of which of the following embryologic structures?
explanation_html:
Educational Objective: This patient has been identified to have a horseshoe kidney on a CT scan of the abdomen. Abnormal migration and fusion of the metanephric blastema is the most likely cause of this patient’s findings.

Key Concept: The metanephric blastema is the embryonic mesenchymal tissue that leads to the development of the kidney.

Explanation: The metanephric blastema arises from the intermediate mesoderm, which ultimately differentiates into all epithelial cell types of the nephron. This includes structures such as the proximal tubules, distal tubules, and podocytes. A horseshoe kidney can form when the metanephric blastema abnormally migrates and fuses.

Differential: This patient has been found to have a horseshoe kidney after completion of a CT scan of the abdomen. A horseshoe kidney results from abnormal migration and fusion of the metanephric blastema, whereas defects of the mesonephric duct or tubules affect genital tract development, the ureteric bud affects the collecting system without causing renal fusion, and the urachus is unrelated to kidney formation.

Incorrect Answers: A, B, D, and E.

Choice A: Mesonephric duct is incorrect. The mesonephric duct is derived from the intermediate mesoderm and plays an important role in the development of the urogenital system. Abnormal migration and fusion of the metanephric blastema is more likely the cause of the patient’s horseshoe kidney.

Choice B: Mesonephric tubules is incorrect. The mesonephric tubules ultimately develop into the efferent ducts of the epididymis in males and degenerate in females. The patient’s horseshoe kidney most likely resulted from abnormal migration and fusion of the metanephric blastema.

Choice D: Urachus is incorrect. The urachus is an embryonic tubular structure that connects from the dome of the bladder to the umbilicus. This structure normally is obliterated during fetal development and becomes the median umbilical ligament.

Choice E: Ureteric bud is incorrect. The ureteric bud is an aspect of the mesonephric duct that initiates definitive kidney development. The ureteric bud ultimately gives rise to the collecting ducts, calyces, renal pelvis, and ureter.
